beats.text: Planes don't leave smoke. They leave clouds.
Burning fuel makes water. Hot steam, blasting out the back.
Up there, the air is minus fifty.
The steam hits that cold and freezes into tiny ice crystals, like your breath on a cold day.
That's the white line you see. A thin cloud of ice, not smoke.
If the air is dry, it fades fast. If it's humid, it stays and spreads.
Fly low, and there's no trail. The air is too warm.
